_comment: DIRECTORY (the license lookup) — the API-driven alternative to the flat projects.json.
One record per OpenAI ChatGPT Edu user = one 'license' the helpdesk tracks in their CMDB.
The only question this answers: given a username, which fund/org pays for that seat?
OpenAI usage carries no project/tag attributes, so a user maps to exactly ONE fund_org.
OpenChargeback calls this per user seen in the monthly usage export:  GET user -> fund_org.
The API NEVER answers empty: any username not listed here resolves to master_fund_org below,
so a charge is always attributable to *something*. Whether that something can actually take
the charge is finance's call at journal time, not ours — an overdrawn or closed fund is theirs
to re-home downstream. We only guarantee every charge lands on a real code.
KNOWN LIMITATION (accepted): this lookup has no time dimension. It returns the fund_org that is
current when billing runs, and that fund_org takes the WHOLE month. A mid-month reassignment is
not pro-rated — the new fund/org gets the entire month. There is no way to ask what a user's
fund/org was on a given date, so we don't try; finance re-homes anything that lands wrong.
Vendor-neutral: the helpdesk exposes it as an API; the shape below is the contract, not the
storage. fund_org is a code that joins to fund-orgs.example.json.
This file is a worked EXAMPLE populated with the Northwinds faculty/staff directory.

licenses._note: Dept head. A Principal Invoicee of the CS dept fund AND a user of it — a manager can be a user.
Dept finance admin; dept covers her seat.
Non-grant teaching faculty — the department picks up her AI use. Dept head is invoiced, not her.
Research PI (ML/LLM). Charges his own seat to his grant; also the Principal Invoicee for his lab's seats.
Transom lab. Never invoiced directly; usage rolls up to Transom, itemized by user.
Systems PI. Charges to a discretionary/gift fund rather than a sponsored award.
Second research group, a different department — shows the model isn't CS-specific.
